name: What is the best order to build an ADU kitchen?

mainEntity.name: What sequence should contractors follow when constructing an ADU kitchen from rough-in to finish?
mainEntity.text: What sequence should contractors follow when constructing an ADU kitchen from rough-in to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most efficient ADU kitchen build follows a predictable sequence so the later finishes fit properly and inspections happen on time. First come framing changes and any structural corrections needed for the layout. Then the plumber and electrician complete rough-ins for the sink, cooking appliance, outlets, lighting, and ventilation. After those systems pass inspection, insulation and drywall can go in. Flooring is installed either before cabinets or around them depending on the material and project strategy, but that decision should be made early. Cabinets are then set and leveled, followed by countertop templating and fabrication. Once counters are installed, the backsplash, plumbing fixtures, appliances, and trim finish the space. If this sequence gets out of order, the project can run into measurement problems, inspection delays, or expensive rework. A good contractor keeps the kitchen on a tight schedule because many other trades depend on it. In practice, the kitchen is where planning, sequencing, and craftsmanship all show up at once.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is framing adjustments, plumbing and electrical rough-in, inspections, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinets, countertops, backsplash, appliances, and final trim. The sequence matters because cabinets and counters depend on completed rough-ins and accurate measurements before installation.
